page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-112 is a compute-optimized instance provisioned on dedicated third-generation AMD EPYC 7B13 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the system provides 112 vCPUs derived from 56 physical cores running two threads per core. Memory allocation totals 448 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include vector extensions up to AVX, hardware acceleration for AES, VAES, and SHA cryptographic routines, and bit-manipulation instruction sets. The instance includes no bundled local storage disks and does not feature dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory access performance. Multi-threaded evaluations highlight top-tier rankings in stress-ng multi-core testing (164,277.47) and PassMark CPU scoring (94,624.64), with top-decile results in cryptographic and physics computations. Geekbench ray tracing performance reaches 112,317.0 points, alongside high cached read bandwidth of 7,743.53 GB/sec and uncached read throughput of 273.18 GB/sec. In-memory data structures perform strongly, generating over 120 million Redis SET operations per second and 48.38 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Tradeoffs emerge in single-threaded workloads and heavy machine learning execution. Single-core Geekbench (1,666.0) and compression scores land in median percentiles due to lower base per-core clock frequencies relative to low-density compute models. Additionally, without AVX-512 extensions or dedicated GPU acceleration, large language model generation slows down considerably on large parameter models, achieving only 2.74 tokens per second on 70B parameter architectures.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-standard-112 delivers dense multi-threaded computation per allocated core, maximizing throughput for horizontally scalable tasks. The instance is suited for high-density compilation, batch processing, electronic design automation, continuous integration pipelines, static web distribution clusters, and distributed Redis caches.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-112 is a compute-optimized virtual server configured with 112 vCPUs and 448 GB of RAM, powered by 56 physical cores of AMD EPYC 7B13 processors on the x86_64 architecture. The server allocates a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core and includes hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA cryptography, though it provides no integrated local storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top tier for multi-core compute throughput, highlighted by elevated PassMark CPU and stress-ng multi-core scores, alongside strong uncached memory read bandwidth of 273.18 GB/sec and Redis SET performance surpassing 120 million operations per second. Lower single-core burst throughput and the absence of AVX-512 restrict deep learning generation efficiency. The server delivers reliable resource density for large-scale code compilation, continuous integration build farms, distributed in-memory databases, and high-concurrency web serving workloads.
